About Me

Peer Support Specialist • Developer • Open-Source Advocate

Hello, I'm Markus 👋

I'm a peer support specialist and developer based in Iowa City, Iowa (Eastern Iowa's I-380 Corridor). My work lives at the intersection of mental health recovery and open-source technology — two worlds that share more values than you'd think: transparency, collaboration, lived experience, and the belief that the best tools are the ones you can inspect, fork, and make your own.

Peer Support Work 🌱

I'm employed at Shelter House Iowa as a Senior Fresh Starts Janitor and Peer Support Specialist, working out of 501 Southgate in Iowa City. I'm also a Fairweather Lodge graduate — meaning I've walked the path I now help others navigate.

Independently, I operate Corridor Peer Pathways — an open-source, community-maintained peer support resource and living map for mental health & crisis recovery across Johnson and Linn Counties.

What I bring to peer support:

  • Lived experience — I've been through the system. That's not a footnote, it's the foundation.
  • Goal-setting & accountability — Walking alongside, not directing from above
  • Resource navigation — Connecting people with real, local, current resources
  • Community reintegration — Helping people find their footing and their people
  • Documentation — Because recovery knowledge shouldn't disappear when someone moves on

Development Work 💻

I build tools that reflect the values I practice in peer support: transparent, inspectable, and designed to empower the people using them.

  • HALLway — A NixOS-based operating system stack built around privacy-first, local-first computing. Your digital life should live on your hardware, under your rules.
  • Corridor Peer Pathways — Open-source peer support resources for Eastern Iowa, including 70+ verified organizations and field-tested frameworks.
  • socialize.sh — Exploring what your camera app's Social Media depth features really do with your photos and metadata.
  • This site — A living portfolio, blog, and starter kit built with Eleventy, Bulma, and Sass.

The Thread That Connects It All 🧵

People sometimes ask how peer support and programming fit together. The answer is simple: they're the same work.

Both are about building systems that respect the people inside them. Both require transparency, patience, and the willingness to document what you've learned so the next person doesn't have to start from scratch. Both believe that the best solutions come from lived experience shared freely.

Recovery was never meant to be proprietary. Neither was good software.

Why This Site Exists 🎯

  1. Portfolio — Showcase my projects in peer support and technology
  2. Blog/Devlog — Share thoughts, tutorials, and progress updates
  3. Bridge — Connect the peer support and open-source communities
  4. Starter Kit — Provide a real, working example others can learn from and fork
  5. Digital Home — A living space on the web that evolves with me

The "Finger File" Tradition 🫰💢👉

This site is inspired by the classic Unix finger protocol from the 90s. Developers like John Carmack would maintain a .plan file — a simple text document showing what they were working on. It was personal, direct, and authentic.

This site carries that spirit forward: a personal status file for the modern web.
